1.explanation:
1. CreateAppendKeyboardBindings.js: The handler for the “a” key only triggers appendElement when exactly one element is selected and never falls back to createElement if append isn’t possible. To satisfy the design (append or fallback to create), this binding must detect when append fails and call createElement instead.  
2. CreateAppendEditorActions.js: The appendElement action always calls contextPad.triggerEntry('append') and does nothing if there is no append entry. It must be extended to detect an empty append menu (via popupMenu.isEmpty or contextPad.getContextPadEntries) and trigger createElement in that case.  
3. AppendRules.js: Currently append is disallowed on a SubProcess with triggeredByEvent (i.e. an Event Sub‐Process). This rule prevents the append menu from ever appearing on an Event Sub‐Process. Removing or adjusting this rule will allow the append menu to show for Event Sub‐Processes, fulfilling the primary append case.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows a simple BPMN model with a Start Event (“hunger noticed”) connected to a Task (“choose recipe”) feeding into an Event Sub‐Process (a square with a double border and an “X” marker). The context pad for the Event Sub‐Process is open, showing tools for connecting, deleting, editing, but no “append” (+) button. Pressing the “a” key (the append shortcut) does nothing even though append should fall back to “create” when no append menu is available.
